Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 12, a relatively short one coming off the preseason opener: - Think we're at a point where the Kyle Shanahan updates are not needed here. He's essentially back doing everything, though not yet calling plays in during practice. If and when there's something new on this front, we'll note it. - Here's the list of Saturday's non participants: RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness/tendinitis), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), QB Kurtis Rourke (undisclosed/ribs), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), WR KhaDarel Hodge (undisclosed), CB Nate Hobbs (groin), LB Dre Greenlaw (appeared to be a rest day). Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) - WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain) was back in the practice and made a couple of plays, including hauling in a deep ball from QB Mac Jones late in the session. - CB Jack Jones (hand) was back at practice after hurting that hand in the Titans game. Marques Sigle (oblique) was also back and participating. - Hodge was doing some work on the side, along with many of the others. For the first time I've seen since his injury, James was doing work on the side by taking handoffs and doing some running. Rourke was in street clothes but watching the session from the side. It's unclear exactly what the diagnosis was after he left the hospital. - As you might expect given that so many of the backups played a lot of snaps less than 48 hours ago, the reps for this practice largely went to the 1s and 2s. - Perhaps the most notable development of the day was the addition of rookie Carver Willis to the LG competition. Willis got a look with the top unit Saturday as Jones got some work at right guard. And Austen Pleasants also got a few reps at LG. Trent Williams called it a "three-man race," an indication that this thing is still wide open. That speaks to the fact that nobody is separating here and I would suggest, again, that the starting LG may not be on the roster right now. - DT Osa Odighizuwa certainly didn't help those guys with his performance today. He was all over the place, beating whichever guard was in his way multiple times, including Willis on his first rep with the 1s. - A Deebo note from Trent Williams' post practice presser: Williams said on the game broadcast he thinks this could be Deebo's best year. Asked why he said that today, Williams pointed to Deebo having a bit of a chip on his shoulder: "Everybody knows as soon as you see him, he's in different type of shape," Williams said. "Probably the best shape I've seen him in since I've known him. And I know he's coming from a situation where he feels people doubt his ability and [I] think he's a dangerous player without anybody doubting him. So you put that extra doubt to him, that extra fuel to his fire, I think he's going to be a lot better." - Jones once again got his hands on the ball early in practice as DT James Thompson Jr. stuffed a run by Khalil Herbert. It was unclear if Thompson or Jones forced the fumble but Jones recovered it. Thompson has, to me, been one of this camp's most pleasant surprises and continues to build a case for a spot on the 53. - With Greenlaw resting, Jaden Dugger got to work alongside Fred Warner at WIL some more. The Niners are clearly intrigued with Dugger and his versatility. Just me handicapping it right now, he seems like the favorite to be the "fever" backer but still a long way to go before Week 1. - Some offensive highlights today: Mac Jones maneuvering in the pocket to hit WR De'Zhaun Stribling over the middle for a big gain... QB Brock Purdy fired a perfect ball down over the middle to Mike Evans who was closely covered by Deommodore Lenoir. It was in a spot only Evans could catch it and kept him out of harm's way for an approaching safety... QB Adrian Martinez hit WR Deebo Samuel for a big gain on a deep crosser... Purdy dropped another one in the bucket on a deep corner for WR Trenton Irwin for a big gain and found TE Luke Farrell for a big gain down the seam. - Some defensive highlights today: Lots of pressure it seemed from the DL with Odighizuwa leading the way. Also had Romello Height down for a would-be sack when he attacked the B gap and blew past Colby... Lenoir was sticky in coverage even when he allowed a completion but he also had a PBU on a throw for Demarcus Robinson from Purdy... Thompson and Bryson Eason had would-be sacks or at least pressures against G Kion Smith... S Jalen Stroman made a good read on a Jones throw for Robinson and jumped in front of it for an interception he likely would have scored on. - That'll do it for today. Niners are back at it tomorrow then have a joint practice with the Chargers in LA. I'll be there for that one so we'll have plenty to cover coming up. Thanks for reading and enjoy your Saturday.
